source.readingNote: Independent reviewer Codex — codex-c83e7a read all 23 published pages and all 188 original items, checked the recorded PDF SHA-256, and inspected page images for formulas and typography. Earlier workers’ source-specific readings are retained with attribution. This review adds three items, independently reads the original Hochster 2002 modification/denominator passages and the later Datta–Murayama DVR counterexample, and corrects the packet in place.

summary: André proves finite direct summands over Noetherian regular rings, balanced big Cohen–Macaulay existence, faithfully flat domination of finite covers, and a restricted CM descent theorem. The proof uses normalized Kummer almost flatness, the companion perfectoid Abhyankar lemma, Ext descent and algebra modifications. Independent review corrects statement boundaries and ownership, records 191 items (23 library, 9 planned, 159 missing) in seven routes, and verifies 25 source findings: 20 confirmed, five rejected. The main theorems retain corrected proofs; the appendix’s noncomplete pure-to-split claim is false in general and replaced by its complete-base repair. This is a source extraction and routing plan, not a claim of formalization.

items.name: Purity survives local Noetherian completion
items.statement: If R→S is a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, the induced map between their maximal-ideal-adic completions is pure.
items.note: For an arbitrary finite presented Rhat-module N and an element killed after tensoring with Shat, reduce modulo m^n. The Rhat-module N/m^nN is an R/m^n-module and purity of R→S gives injectivity before completing. This injection remains injective after n_S-adic completion because S is Noetherian, N/m^nN is finite over R, its tensor with S is finite over S, and Krull intersection applies. The original element therefore lies in every m^nN, hence is zero by Krull intersection over Rhat. This tests every finite presented Rhat-module; no descent of N to R is assumed. The rings are Noetherian and the map local.

items.name: Almost base and almost-zero modules
items.statement: An almost base is a commutative ring V with an idempotent ideal m for which m⊗_V m is V-flat. A V-module M is almost zero when mM=0; almostification is the Serre quotient by these modules.

items.name: Completed cyclotomic Witt-fraction field is perfectoid
items.statement: For perfect k of characteristic p, let K_0=Frac(W(k)), choose compatible primitive p^j-th roots ζ_(p^j), and put K_∞=∪_j K_0(ζ_(p^j)). Its valuation completion is a perfectoid field.

items.name: Integral model of a perfectoid Weierstrass localization
items.statement: Let C be a spectral perfectoid algebra over a perfectoid field and let f,ϖ admit compatible p-power roots, with ϖ a pseudouniformizer and f power bounded. The canonical map from the ϖ-adic completion of C°[(f/ϖ^i)^(1/p^∞)] to C{f/ϖ^i}° is an almost isomorphism for the valuation almost ideal.
items.note: The cited input is Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.4(ii), read in the published version (p.281): for U = U(f_1,…,f_n/g) ⊆ Spa(R^♭, R^(♭+)) rational with f_i, g ∈ R^(♭°) and f_n = ϖ^(♭N), O_X(U)°^a = R°⟨(f_1^♯/g^♯)^(1/p^∞),…,(f_n^♯/g^♯)^(1/p^∞)⟩^a. André applies it to numerators f_i^♭, ϖ^(♭i) and denominator ϖ^(♭i). This is why f_i must be an untilt (tube-sharp-approximation). The conclusion is an almost isomorphism, not an equality of integral rings.

items.name: Normalized two-index Kummer tower
items.statement: Fix perfect k of characteristic p, A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]], 0≠g∈A, and compatible cyclotomic and coordinate roots. Infinite indices mean directed unions; hats mean separated p-adic completion of the integral ring, followed on the generic algebra by inverting p.
items.note: The adjoining-root quotient is not silently identified with its normalization A_jk°. For k>0 even A_jk need not be a domain. Use the full coordinate-root tower displayed here. The abbreviated identity in §0.6 omits coordinate roots (E25), while §§2.2–2.3 include them.

items.name: Recovering an integral splitting from Artinian quotients
items.statement: For finite A⊂B with A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]], splittings modulo every I_m=(p^m,T_1^(p^m),…,T_n^(p^m)), m≥1, imply an A-linear splitting A→B.

Artinian does not mean a finite underlying set when k is infinite. Original transition maps need not be surjective. Completeness of finite B is unnecessary for the last step: Hom_A(B,−) commutes with the target inverse limit.
proofSteps: The parameter ideals are descending, m_A-primary and cofinal with the maximal-ideal powers, by parameter-quotient-cofinality.
For each m, view retractions as H_m={f∈Hom_A(B,A/I_m):f(1)=1}. A finite generating family of B embeds this Hom module in a finite power of A/I_m.
Apply retraction-coset-stabilization to the quotient transitions. Eventual ranges are nonempty and the restricted transitions are surjective by the two cited Mathlib suppliers.
Use countable-surjective-system-section, then compatible-functional-limit and A≅lim_m A/I_m. The resulting functional has value 1 on 1.

items.name: Big CM algebras over a regular local base are faithfully flat
items.statement: If A is Noetherian regular local and C is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay A-algebra, C is faithfully flat over A.
items.note: Do not assume C finitely generated. Use bounded projective dimension of finite A-modules and a Tor dimension-shifting argument; finite-module Auslander–Buchsbaum alone does not prove this. The footnote on p.87 prints M where N is required in two Tor terms (E6); the corrected proof explicitly retains the associated-prime embedding supplier.
proofSteps: Every finite module over the d-dimensional regular local ring A has projective dimension ≤d, so Tor_i(M,C)=0 for i>d.
Descend on i>0. By a prime filtration it suffices to take M=A/P. Choose a maximal A-regular sequence x in P; the Cohen–Macaulay quotient N=A/(x) has P as an associated prime, giving A/P→N.
Extend x to parameters; balanced big CM makes x regular on C, hence Tor_i(N,C)=0 for every i>0 by the Koszul resolution.
The exact segment Tor_(i+1)(N/M,C)→Tor_i(M,C)→Tor_i(N,C) has zero outer terms by induction and regularity. Thus the middle term vanishes.
The flatness criterion for all finite modules and m_A C≠C give faithful flatness.

proofSteps: The larger exponents make the ideals descending. Since p^m≥m, every stated generator is in m_A^m.

items.name: Mittag–Leffler stabilization of retraction cosets
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, let I_m be descending ideals with each A/I_m Artinian, let B be a finitely generated A-module and e∈B. Assume H_m={f∈Hom_A(B,A/I_m):f(e)=1} is nonempty for every m≥1. Reduction induces an inverse system H_m. For each m the images of H_l→H_m, l≥m, eventually stabilize.
items.locator: Hochster, Contracted ideals from integral extensions of regular rings (1973), p.30, retraction sets H_k and their images; used by André §3.4
proofSteps: Evaluation on a finite set of generators embeds Hom_A(B,A/I_m) in (A/I_m)^q, so it is an Artinian A-module.
H_m is a nonempty coset of the submodule of functionals vanishing on e. The image from H_l is a coset of the image of that submodule.
These direction submodules form a descending chain inside the fixed Artinian target, hence stabilize.
Nested nonempty cosets of the same submodule are equal: any point of the smaller coset also belongs to the larger and identifies both with its translate. Thus the cosets stabilize.
acceptance: The proof applies when the residue fields are infinite.
No original transition H_(m+1)→H_m is assumed surjective.
Finite presentation of B is not used for the evaluation embedding; finite generation suffices.

items.name: Corrected contracting-endomorphism functional criterion
items.statement: Let (R,m) be a nonzero commutative local ring, r∈m, and suppose ∩_(n≥1) r^nR=0 and either r=0 or multiplication by r on R is injective. Let σ:R→R be a local endomorphism with R free as a module over σ(R), and suppose ∩_(j≥0) σ^j(m)R⊆rR. Let R⊂S be a commutative ring extension and τ:S→S an injective endomorphism restricting to σ. If Hom_R(S,R)≠0, there is an R-linear ρ:S→R with ρ(1)=1.
items.locator: Appendix A.3.1(c)⇒(b), pp.90–91, with the explicit additional hypothesis required by E4
proofSteps: Choose a nonzero λ:S→R. If r=0 no division is needed. Otherwise separation bounds the integers n for which λ(S)⊆r^nR; choose the largest. Regularity of r makes division by r^n unique and R-linear, giving λ′ with image not contained in rR.
Precompose with multiplication by an element s whose image is outside rR, so λ′(1)∉rR.

Choose j with λ′(1)∉σ^j(m)R. Injectivity of τ implies that of σ. Iterating freeness makes R free over σ^j(R). In a basis expansion, one coefficient of λ′(1) is a unit of the local ring σ^j(R). A scaled coordinate functional μ:R→σ^j(R) sends λ′(1) to 1.
Define ρ=(σ^j:R≅σ^j(R))^(-1)∘μ∘λ′∘τ^j. Semilinearity of τ^j and σ^j(R)-linearity of μ show R-linearity; evaluation at 1 gives 1.
acceptance: The r=0 case is retained, including the equal-characteristic application.
The square-zero example R=k[[t]][ε]/ε², S=k[[t]]⋉εk((t)), r=ε is excluded by the added regularity disjunction.
No multiplicativity of ρ, finite generation of S or Noetherianity of R is introduced.

proofSteps: Identify H_m^d(M) with M⊗_R E.
Curry Hom_R(M⊗E,E) to Hom_R(M,End_R(E)).
Use End_R(E)≅Rhat and the zero-detection property.

items.name: A pure extension of a complete Noetherian local base splits
items.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring and S a commutative R-algebra. If R→S is pure, there is an R-linear map ρ:S→R with ρ(1)=1. Neither regularity, integrality, finite generation of S nor an endomorphism of S is required.
items.locator: Corrected complete-base branch of André A.3.1; direct proof from Hochster Local cohomology (2011), Theorem 5.1
proofSteps: Purity makes E→S⊗_R E, e↦1⊗e, injective.
Injectivity of E extends id_E across this injection to f:S⊗E→E.
Currying gives S→End_R(E)≅R; at 1 the image is id_E, corresponding to 1.
acceptance: Applies to an arbitrary pure algebra over Z_p.
A finite algebra assumption is unnecessary.
For a noncomplete base the construction gives a map S→Rhat extending R→Rhat, not necessarily a retraction to R.

items.statement: Let B be a complete mixed-characteristic local domain, finite over A=V[[x_2,…,x_d]], with V a complete DVR and x_1 its uniformizer. Apply the assumed retraction; the nonzero socle monomial in A_e/(y_1^q,…,y_d^q) gives a contradiction.

items.name: Extending the contracting power-series endomorphism
items.statement: Let A=V[[x_2,…,x_d]] with V a complete DVR and q≥2. The continuous V-endomorphism σ(x_i)=x_i^q extends to an automorphism of A+. A is finite free over σ(A), with monomial basis whose exponents are <q, and ∩_j σ^j(m_A)A=πA.

Extend the automorphism to its fraction field and then to an algebraic closure.
The integral closure of that union agrees with A+; restrict the field automorphism.
Group power-series exponents by residues modulo q for freeness; shrinking coordinate powers give the stated intersection.

items.name: Integral closures in the normalized Kummer tower

items.name: Artin–Rees lemma
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal, M a finite R-module and N a submodule. There is k such that for every n ≥ k, I^n M ∩ N = I^(n−k)(I^k M ∩ N).

items.name: Krull intersection theorem
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, J an ideal and M a finite R-module. An element x ∈ M lies in ⋂_n J^n M if and only if (1 − r)x = 0 for some r ∈ J. In particular ⋂_n J^n = 0 when R is local and J is proper.

items.name: Nakayama's lemma
items.statement: Let R be a ring, I an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical and N a finitely generated R-module. If N ⊆ I N then N = 0.

items.name: Faithful flatness by proper ideals
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if and only if it is flat and I M ≠ M for every proper ideal I of R. For a local ring R it suffices that M be flat and m_R M ≠ M.
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean:73. The local form follows because every proper ideal lies in m_R.

items.name: Partial algebra modification of degree n
items.statement: Use the pointed-module specialization needed in §4: a B-module M with distinguished element e (the image of 1 under a specified B→M), parameters x_1,…,x_d, a relation x_(i+1)u=Σ_(j≤i)x_j u_j and n≥1. Put F=u−Σ_(j≤i)(x_j e)T_j in M⊗_B B[T_1,…,T_i]. Define M′=M[T]_(≤n)/(F·B[T]_(≤n−1)), with map M→M′ from constant polynomials and distinguished image of e. Then the image of u lies in (x_1,…,x_i)M′.
items.locator: §4.1, p.85; Hochster 2002 §4.1, p.8 of author preprint; Heitmann–Ma §1.2
items.note: E16 corrects the multiplier ring to B[T], independently checked in Hochster’s original §4.1. The formal contract also makes the distinguished element explicit; a bare arbitrary module has no coefficient 1. All applications begin with the algebra B and preserve the image of 1. No multiplication of two arbitrary module-valued polynomials is used.

items.name: Hochster's criterion for a Cohen–Macaulay algebra for (B, x)
items.statement: For a nonzero Noetherian local B and a fixed system of parameters x, a B-algebra C with m_B C≠C on which x is regular exists if and only if there is no bad finite pointed partial-modification sequence beginning at B. Construct C by iterated full algebra modifications killing all parameter relations, and use finite partial-module approximations to detect improperness.

items.note: The full algebra construction carries its multiplication from algebra quotients and algebra colimits. Iterate the simultaneous killing of all relations, then take the countable colimit; any relation appears at a finite stage. A bad witness uses finitely many variables, relations and degrees, hence yields a bad partial sequence. Conversely a map to a big CM algebra extends through full modifications and prevents badness. For the two-ring statement use the double-sequence criterion, Hochster 2002 Theorem 4.2, p.9.

items.name: Hochster's denominator lemma
items.statement: Let M be a pointed B-module with element e, T a B-algebra, c∈T a non-zero-divisor and α:M→T[1/c] B-linear with α(e)=1 and α(M)⊆c^(−N)T. Suppose c kills each parameter colon obstruction in T: x_(i+1)t_(i+1)=Σ_(j≤i)x_j t_j implies c t_(i+1)∈(x_1,…,x_i)T. For a pointed partial modification of degree D, α extends to β:M′→T[1/c] with β(e′)=1 and β(M′)⊆c^(−(ND+D+N))T.

A degree-D monomial has denominator at most N+D(N+1). The bound is independent of the specific relations, as needed for arbitrarily deep roots of π. items.name: An almost Cohen–Macaulay algebra excludes bad sequences
items.statement: If D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, π^(1/p^∞)), then no finite sequence of partial modifications of B relative to (B, x) is bad. More precisely, for every sequence B = M_1 → ⋯ → M_ℓ of degree ≤ n and every h there is m such that B → D extends to maps M_t → π^(−1/p^h)D compatible along the sequence, so the image of 1 in M_ℓ is not in m_B M_ℓ.

A bad sequence would force π^(1/p^h)∈m_B D for every h, contradicting almost CM. Thus the distinguished image of 1 survives. items.name: Equal-characteristic perfect-closure trace argument
items.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p>0, R=k[[T_0,…,T_n]], and R⊂S a finite extension of domains with fraction fields Galois of group G and S^G=R. A coefficient projection of a suitable trace multiple therefore yields an R-linear retraction S→R.

items.statement: There exists an excellent Henselian DVR V of characteristic p>0 with Hom_V(V^(1/p),V)=0. assessmentHistory.assessment: Reconstructed independently from the printed hypotheses on p. 90, which are exactly: R local with maximal ideal m, not necessarily noetherian; r in m with R r-adically separated; sigma a local endomorphism of R with R free over sigma(R) and the intersection over m of sigma^m(m).R contained in rR; and S an extension of R to which sigma extends as an injective endomorphism. All four hold for the example. R = k[[t]][e]/(e^2) is local with maximal ideal (t,e) and r = e lies in it; R is e-adically separated because e^2 = 0, so the intersection of the e^n R is already 0 at n = 2; sigma, sending t to t^2 and fixing e and k, is local because sigma(m) lies in (t^2,e), and R is free over sigma(R) with basis 1, t since k[[t]] = k[[t^2]] + t k[[t^2]]; sigma^j(m).R = (t^{2^j}, e)R, whose intersection over j is eA = rR, so the containment holds with equality; and S = A + eK with (a,b)(c,d) = (ac, ad+bc) contains R coefficientwise as a subring, with sigma extending by the same formula, injectively because a(t) -> a(t^2) is injective on k((t)). Condition (c) holds: lambda(a + eb) := ea is additive, satisfies lambda(rho x) = rho lambda(x) for rho = c + ed because both sides equal eca, and lambda(1) = e is non-zero. Condition (b) fails: a retraction rho would have rho(e) = e, but for every N one has e = t^N (e t^{-N}) with e t^{-N} in S, so rho(e) lies in every t^N R, and the intersection of those is 0 since A is t-adically separated; hence rho(e) = 0. Two additions to the record. First, the example also refutes (c) => (a), not only (c) => (b): since tK = K one has tS = tA + eK, so S/tS = A/tA = k while R/tR = k + ek, and the class of e dies, so for the finitely presented P = R/tR the map P -> P tensor_R S is not injective and R -> S is not pure. Second, the point of failure is sharper than 'division by a zero divisor is ill defined'. Here lambda(S) = eA = rR exactly, so the proof's opening step - divide lambda by a power of r until some value escapes rR - is called for, and it is impossible: lambda = r lambda' with lambda' R-linear would force e lambda'(1) = e, hence lambda'(1) = 1 + ed, a unit, and then lambda'(1)^{-1} lambda' would be the retraction just shown not to exist. The obstruction is thus the impossibility of a single division, which r-adic separation cannot address, since separation only excludes an infinite descent. Containment, supporting the finding's judgement that the main theorem is untouched: both applications the paper itself makes of (c) => (b) satisfy the repair proposed. The characteristic p application takes r = 0, where the step is vacuous because rR = 0 and a non-zero lambda already has a value outside it; the mixed-characteristic application takes R = V[[T_1,...,T_n]] with r a uniformiser of a discrete valuation ring, a non-zerodivisor in a domain. The example's R is non-reduced and its S is not module-finite, so nothing in sections 0 to 4 is affected.
